Overview

CoinTracker is on a mission to unlock everyone's financial potential so they can build the life they want. We started with crypto, building the tax and portfolio tools that millions of users trust to trade digital assets with peace of mind. Nino builds the next layer of financial fluency for our users. Nino is an AI-powered financial operating system that makes comprehensive, expert-level tax and financial planning advice accessible.

More on Nino: Comprehensive tax and financial planning strategies are currently locked behind high AUM fees or require enough wealth to have a family office. We are turning expert judgment into software so we can serve millions. AI is going to redefine how people understand their finances and how tax advice gets delivered. Not in ten years, in 2026. You can help define that, or spend the next few years adapting to rules someone else wrote. Nino sits inside CoinTracker ($100M raised, partnered with Coinbase, TurboTax, H&R Block, and Thomson Reuters) with the autonomy of an early-stage startup and the reach of an established platform.

 

Your mission

As Tax Lead, you'll own a book of roughly 50 Nino clients end-to-end: preparing, reviewing, and filing their returns and giving them proactive, white-glove tax advice.

Most of your time goes to client and compliance work, using our in-house AI tools alongside traditional tax software.

Along the way, you'll share what you learn with our engineers, so the logic in your head (ISO exercises, AMT crossover points, multi-state allocation, Roth conversions) makes our AI smarter for every household after yours. Product experience is a plus.

When we're done, the tax planning advice we'll provide won't just be static advice delivered once a quarter. It will execute, perform, and action personalized advice to each customer in a way that is simply not possible with legacy tax planning.

Location: U.S. remote.

Your one-year outcomes

  • Manage 50 to 60 clients end-to-end with excellence.

What you will do

  • Interface with Clients: Proactive tax insights and white-glove experience.

  • Prepare, review, and file tax returns for households (starting with those in $1M – $25M net worth) plus related business returns.

  • Share your tax logic: relay learnings from client work so engineers can turn your reasoning into product.

  • Review AI output: check and correct AI-generated advice before it reaches your clients.

  • Solve Edge Cases: AMT crossover, wash sales, multi-state allocation, QSBS, pass-through optimization.

What we look for

  • Role-agnostic

    • Opportunity alignment: You want to bring expert tax and financial advice to households that have outgrown doing it themselves, and you want to do it at an early-stage company where your work moves the number.

    • High agency: You see what needs doing and do it. You don't wait for a brief, a budget, or an engineer.

    • Exceptional collaboration: You make the people around you better: sales, advisors, engineers, and agencies. You say what you think and follow through.

    • First-principles thinking: You start from how customers decide, not from a playbook. You can explain why a number moved.

  • Role-specific

    • 5+ years with an active CPA license. You've prepared, reviewed, and/or filed 500+ individual (1040) returns.

    • You've served clients with $1M – $25M net worth.

    • You have working knowledge of business returns (S-corps, partnerships, Schedule C, LLC).

    • You know the tax code, not just the tax software. You research ambiguous positions using primary sources (IRC, Treasury Regs, Rev. Rulings, case law) and can defend them.

    • You're AI native, with hands-on use of AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT.

    • Bonus: you're a tax attorney or CFP, or you have experience with trusts and estate planning.

The starting salary for this position is between $137,000 - $197,000 USD. Candidate's location does not impact the posted salary range. The level for this role, and where an offer falls within this range, is set by experience.

The actual compensation offered will be based on a variety of job-related factors including relevant skills, education, and experience. This position also includes equity in CoinTracker and benefits like medical, dental, vision, 401(k), life insurance, and PTO.

descriptions.job-1ur924y:
About Polygon Labs

Polygon Labs is a global blockchain payments company building and operating infrastructure to move money instantly, reliably, and at internet scale, with the mission to move all money onchain. It is building the Polygon Open Money Stack, an open and integrated stack of services and technologies to instantly and reliably move money anywhere, and put it to work. Its infrastructure has facilitated trillions of dollars in onchain value transfer and supported millions of transactions daily for some of the globe's largest banks, fintechs, enterprises, and consumer applications.

Your Role

Coinme's BSA/AML Officer is the designated officer accountable for the company's anti-money laundering and sanctions compliance program across consumer, kiosk, and platform-partner channels. You own the program end to end: the risk assessment, the controls that implement it, the monitoring and investigations operation that runs it, and the regulatory relationships that judge it.

This is a player-coach role. You set program design and risk appetite with the Chief Compliance Officer, and you keep enough hands-on depth to review an alert, read an on-chain trace, and sign off on a SAR narrative yourself. You build and govern AI-assisted workflows that carry much of the alert and investigation load, and you develop the analysts who operate them. Decisions here must be timely, documented, and defensible to an examiner, and the program must not depend on any single person, including you.

Your Responsibilities

  • Serve as the designated BSA/AML Officer: own the written AML program, its board and senior-management reporting, and personal accountability for its design and effectiveness under the Bank Secrecy Act and its MSB implementing rules.

  • Own the enterprise BSA/AML and sanctions risk assessment across products, channels (kiosk, retail cash, app, platform partners), geographies, and customer types, and keep controls mapped to it as the business changes.

  • Run transaction monitoring as a measured system: scenario and threshold design, tuning against quantified productivity and coverage, below-the-line testing, and documented change control, spanning fiat and on-chain activity.

  • Own SAR decisioning and filing quality: investigation standards, narrative quality, timeliness, continuing-activity reviews, and the confidentiality controls around them. Own CTR, Travel Rule, and recordkeeping obligations.

  • Own sanctions compliance: OFAC and wallet-address screening, list management, true-match escalation, blocking and rejection handling, and reporting.

  • Own KYC, CDD, and EDD standards: customer risk rating, high-risk customer reviews, and policy on account restriction, exit, and reactivation, in partnership with Payments & Risk on the fraud/AML seam.

  • Lead regulatory examinations and partner oversight: state money transmitter exams, sponsor-bank and platform-partner due diligence and audits, independent testing, and remediation tracking to closure.

  • Design and govern AI-native compliance operations: agentic workflows for alert triage, case enrichment, on-chain tracing, narrative drafting, and quality control, with governance to match (human sign-off on every filing and account action, auditable reasoning trails, model validation, and explicit boundaries on what automation may decide).

  • Build and develop the team: hire, coach, and grow AML analysts and investigators, run the company-wide BSA/AML training program, and treat procedures and runbooks as first-class deliverables.

  • Report to the CCO, executives, and the board with metrics beyond filing counts: alert-to-SAR conversion, investigation cycle time, backlog age, exam and audit findings open versus closed, and automation coverage, connecting compliance decisions to growth and partner standing.

Qualifications

  • Experience: 8+ years in BSA/AML or financial crimes compliance, including 3+ years as a BSA Officer, deputy BSA Officer, or head of AML at a money services business, money transmitter, crypto exchange, or fintech with a sponsor bank.

  • Regulatory depth: Working command of the BSA and its MSB rules (AML program, SAR, CTR, Travel Rule, recordkeeping, FinCEN registration), OFAC sanctions requirements, FinCEN and FATF guidance on virtual assets, and state money transmitter expectations.

  • Exam track record: You have led a program through state or federal examinations and sponsor-bank audits, owned the response, and closed findings with evidence.

  • Crypto typology fluency: Kiosk and cash-to-crypto risk, scam and elder-exploitation patterns, mule and structuring behavior, mixer, darknet, and sanctioned-wallet exposure, and the ability to read a blockchain analytics trace yourself.

  • Monitoring and data fluency: Hands-on scenario tuning and model-risk basics; strong SQL; you answer your own questions without waiting on an analyst.

  • AI-native leadership: You have built or governed AI-assisted compliance workflows and can say concretely what you automated, what guardrails you set, and what you kept human. Aptitude is assessed in a working session.

  • Institution building: You document, cross-train, and design programs that pass an exam without you in the room.

  • People leadership: You have hired, developed, and retained analysts and investigators, and led a team through a change in how the work gets done.

  • Judgment: Independence under commercial pressure, conservative and defensible metrics, and clear communication to examiners, executives, and partners alike.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with blockchain analytics (TRM Labs, Chainalysis, Elliptic) and fraud or identity platforms (Sardine, Prove, or similar).

  • Experience with NMLS multistate exams and coordinated state supervision.

  • Experience with FinCEN 314(a) and 314(b) programs and law-enforcement request handling.

  • Experience building with LLM agent frameworks (Claude Code, agent SDKs) or workflow-automation platforms.

  • Modern data-stack familiarity: Snowflake, dbt, product analytics.

  • Certifications (CAMS, CAMS-Audit, CFE, CCI) or a JD or advanced degree in a relevant field.

Polygon Labs Perks

The goal of the Polygon Labs total rewards program is to support the health and well-being of you and your family. Our comprehensive compensation plan includes the following benefits for our full time employees:

  • Remote first global workforce

  • Industry leading Medical, Dental and Vision health insurance*

  • Company matching 401k with 3% match*

  • $1,500 Home Office Set Up Allowance (life-time max)

  • $75 Monthly internet or phone reimbursement

  • Flexible Time Off

  • Company issued laptop

  • Egg freezing, mental health, and employee wellness benefits

*In certain countries medical, dental and vision is fully covered for employees & their dependents. This is country and plan specific.

*401k is for United States employees only

Polygon Labs is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Polygon Labs is committed to treating all people in a way that allows them to maintain their dignity and independence. We believe in integration and equal opportunity. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process and applicants with a disability may request to be accommodated throughout the recruitment process. We will work with all applicants to accommodate their individual accessibility needs.

If you think you have what it takes, but don't necessarily meet every single point on the job description, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit.

Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

About the Role

As a Staff Software Engineer on the Platform team, you will own the technical direction of Alpaca's streaming platform - our Redpanda-based event backbone and the user-facing streaming infrastructure. Platform also owns Authentication, Developer Experience and QA, and AI-Native Engineering. Streaming is roughly two-thirds of the job and where we expect you to become the deepest engineer in the company; across the other three you review the designs, hold an informed opinion, and lead the work where they meet streaming.

This is a Staff role, so we are hiring for direction as much as delivery - the engineer who decides what the streaming platform looks like in two years, writes the RFC that gets three teams to agree, and then builds the hard part. We own client-facing and internal services, maintain shared libraries nearly every team depends on, and manage our own deployments. Most of our time goes into Go, but we also write Helm charts, dig through logs and metrics, and get pulled into a wide variety of problems.

Things You Get To Do

  • Own the architecture of our event streaming platform end to end - Redpanda, the UTS ecosystem, client libraries and user-facing streaming - and set its two-to-three-year direction
  • Lead the shift from batch to event-driven across Alpaca's systems, working with the teams who own them rather than around them
  • Design user-facing streaming at scale: connection fan-out, slow consumers, backpressure, ordering and delivery guarantees, and the failure modes that only show up on a volatile market day
  • Set the standards for event-driven design - schema evolution, topic ownership, replay, idempotency - and own the shared libraries other teams build against, including the cost of versioning and deprecation
  • Shape AuthN/AuthZ direction across Alpaca and lead the work where identity meets streaming: authorizing real-time subscriptions, token lifecycle on long-lived connections, multi-tenant isolation
  • Help shape how Alpaca builds with AI - the schemas, contracts and event streams you own are the substrate our agentic development platform runs on
  • Partner with SRE on chaos testing and game days for the event backbone, and with our QA stream on test tooling and pre-production gates, so resilience is verified rather than assumed
  • Lead through influence rather than authority, and multiply the engineers around you through mentoring, design review, and handing off the work that grows people
  • Join the Platform on-call rotation and act as technical lead during incidents affecting shared infrastructure

Who You Are (must-haves)

  • 8+ years of professional engineering experience, including several years running systems at real scale. You write Go, or have deep experience in another strongly-typed language and will pick it up quickly.
  • You have architected event streaming systems, not just used them - real production depth in Kafka or Redpanda across partitioning, consumer groups, rebalancing, retention and delivery guarantees, and how each breaks under load.
  • You have delivered realtime data to clients at scale (WebSockets, SSE or gRPC streaming) and handled fan-out, slow consumers and backpressure in production.
  • You have driven technical direction across team boundaries without formal authority. You can point to the decisions you owned, the RFCs you wrote, and what happened next.
  • You have built or maintained libraries many teams depend on, and know what backward compatibility and deprecation actually cost.
  • You have mentored senior engineers and left the teams around you better than you found them.
  • You have real depth in at least one adjacent area - identity and access, developer tooling and CI, or testing and resilience - and genuine curiosity about the others.
  • You know Kubernetes beyond the basics: you can write a Helm chart with relative ease, you understand security best practices, and you have job experience or certifications to prove it.
  • You have worked with relational databases - we use PostgreSQL, but we are not picky as long as the fundamentals are solid.
  • You have worked at a startup before - you thrive in ambiguous environments, embrace changing priorities, know when to balance technical debt with speed, and proactively tackle whatever needs to get done without relying on pre-existing processes or documentation.

Who You Might Be (nice-to-haves)

  • You’ve worked with an IDL or binary serialization format (Protobuf, Avro; we use FlatBuffers) and handled schema evolution across many consumers.
  • You have experience with change data capture (Debezium, PeerDB or similar) and understand how Postgres logical replication works.
  • You’ve worked on auth systems - OAuth 2.0, OIDC, JWT lifecycle, Keycloak or Cognito - especially around long-lived connections or machine-to-machine access.
  • You’ve built agentic or AI-native developer tooling, or designed systems meant to be operated by agents rather than only by people.
  • You’ve run chaos engineering or game days, or built the load and fault-injection testing that makes them worth running.
  • You’ve done IaC with Argo CD or Terraform.
  • You have experience with Grafana’s observability stack - Prometheus, Tempo and all the rest. You might have even written a PromQL query for a new alert once or twice.
  • You’ve worked in fintech or another regulated domain and understand how compliance constraints shape architecture.

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

Alpaca is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a diverse workforce.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe’s Professional Services team works with our most strategic users. You will work on the highest visibility projects to provide technical expertise to our customers to help accelerate their knowledge, solution design and integrations with Stripe. This role is responsible for leading strategic conversations and developing plans that will transform the payments and financial infrastructure for leading enterprises. We're building an AI-first team. Using AI to work efficiently, and to deliver faster and better outcomes for our users, will be a key part of this role.

What you’ll do

Responsibilities

  • Plan and execute integration engineering end-to-end, from high-level architecture down to code implementation. This includes conducting discovery sessions with users to understand their goals, parsing out specific use cases, and guiding users to implement high complexity integrations. 
  • Think on your feet and communicate technical concepts, explaining how Stripe works from both a product feature and API architecture perspective. Manage user expectations on timelines and product changes.

  • Apply AI across the engagement lifecycle to reduce manual effort, accelerate delivery, and improve the quality of what we hand to users.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Solution Architecture and Implementation teams to drive client engagement, customer wins, and revenue on behalf of the Professional Services team
  • Collaborate closely with Product and Engineering to proactively identify potential enhancements and new features based on feedback you’ll gather from the field.

  • Strong generalist technical experience, including proficiency in SQL and an understanding of data structures and algorithms.
  • Understanding of the payments domain and API security topics.
  • Be comfortable talking about technical concepts, and explaining how Stripe works, both from a product features and API architecture perspective.

  • Intellectually curious, with great problem solving skills.

About the Team

Security Engineering makes sure Rain is built right. We run our own AI-driven red team against our code, contracts, and cloud, gate pull requests before they merge, and set the baselines for how every system is configured. This role owns blockchain security end to end: the smart contracts on EVM chains, Solana, and Stellar that hold and move customer funds, the keys and multisigs that control them, and the backend services that act on what happens on chain.

You'll be Rain's blockchain security expert. The calls are yours: what's real, how bad it is, and what has to be fixed before a contract ships or an upgrade goes out. You'll work closely with the leads of our Solana, EVM, and blockchain infrastructure teams, hold the line when it matters, and make the case so they agree, not just comply.

What you’ll do

  • Review smart contract changes and upgrades before they ship, across Solidity (EVM), Rust (Solana), and Soroban (Stellar). Find the bug that matters, and often write the fix yourself

  • Run our contract audits end to end: scope them, work with outside auditors, triage findings from audits, our AI red team, and our bug bounty, set severity, and approve the fixes

  • Own admin key and role security: multisig and Safe setups, signing ceremonies, role separation, timelocks, and who can upgrade, pause, or move what

  • Strengthen treasury and fund-flow protections so no single key, signer, or bad transaction can drain money

  • Find the blind spots in our on-chain monitoring: work out what we can't see today, and tell our blockchain detection and response team which detections to build and why

  • Review how our backend reads and reacts to chain events (indexers, event handlers, signing services), so off-chain code can't be tricked by on-chain input

  • Own the upgrade process so every upgrade is done securely: who deploys, from where, and with what checks. Make sure no contract, chain, or customer program gets left behind on an old version, and prove that what's live matches what was reviewed

  • Build the tools that make this repeatable: fuzzing and invariant tests, and simulations of upgrades and admin actions before anyone signs them

  • Lead the technical response when something goes wrong on chain, and own the plan for where blockchain security goes next

  • Deep, hands-on EVM and Solidity, plus real working knowledge of at least one non-EVM chain (Solana or Stellar/Soroban)

  • You've found real bugs in contracts that hold real money, through audits, contests, bounties, or your own team's code. You know a scary-sounding finding from a real one

  • You've designed or run key management for production contracts: multisigs and Safe, KMS or HSM signing, timelocks, and role-based access

  • Fluent with Foundry, fuzzing and invariant testing, transaction simulation, and reading chain state directly

  • You can read TypeScript backend code well enough to follow how it talks to the chain

  • You've owned security decisions. You can tell a senior engineer their design needs to change and keep a good working relationship

  • You'd rather ship a check than write a document, and you use AI tools heavily without trusting them blindly

Bonus attributes:

  • Stablecoin, payments, or card issuing background

  • Public audit reports, audit contest placings, or bug bounty payouts

  • Hands-on response to a live on-chain exploit or key compromise

  • Formal verification or contract static analysis (Certora, Halmos, Slither, or similar)

  • Experience building security scanners or LLM-based review tools

descriptions.job-15ib24y:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

About the role

We're looking for a Blockchain Intelligence Analyst to operate as a high-judgment, high-autonomy individual contributor specializing in transnational criminal organisations. You will use blockchain analytics, open-source and closed-source intelligence, and cryptocurrency attribution to trace the proceeds of drug trafficking, identify the networks that move them, and produce intelligence that helps TRM and its partners disrupt illicit drug activity.

This is not a people-management role. We're looking for an experienced analyst who can independently lead complex investigations, develop high-confidence assessments, uncover novel attribution, and raise the team's tradecraft through technical expertise and example. This role will require proactive work with law enforcement partners, often picking up a stalled investigation, finding what was missed, and linking it to other cases.

You should be equally comfortable tracing funds across blockchains, identifying laundering and cash-out infrastructure, correlating on-chain and off-chain signals, and turning fragmented data into clear, defensible intelligence that enables partners to make informed operational decisions.

The impact you will have

  • Produce finished intelligence on transnational criminal organisations, vendors, facilitators and laundering pathways, including actor profiles, lead packages and attribution assessments suitable for investigative, executive and partner audiences.

  • Lead complex end-to-end blockchain investigations from initial seed indicators, such as addresses, transactions, exchange exposure and infrastructure leads, through to full attribution.

  • Trace illicit proceeds across multiple blockchains, bridges, mixers, peel chains and nested services, identifying controllers, counterparties and cash-out points, including OTC desks, ATM networks and cash-to-crypto services.

  • Correlate on-chain activity with OSINT, closed-source intelligence and off-chain identity or infrastructure signals to build a complete picture of how transnational criminal organisations operate and move value.

  • Own investigative work-streams from discovery through validation and written production, drafting intelligence that is source-cited, auditable and operationally useful.

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with law enforcement partners, so that our intelligence reflects real investigative tradecraft and gets used.

  • Help strengthen TRM's transnational criminal organisations coverage by contributing new attributions, refining investigative methodology and improving repeatable workflows.

  • Support briefings, partner engagements and capability-building sessions where tracing and attribution tradecraft must be explained clearly and credibly.

What success looks like

  • You generate meaningful attribution and investigative leads in cases where the answers are not obvious and the financial trail is deliberately obscured.

  • You consistently produce finished intelligence that partners trust and use.

  • Your work helps TRM and its partners move faster on high-priority narcotics activity without sacrificing rigor, auditability or defensibility.

  • You improve team capability by mentoring peers, refining tradecraft and strengthening repeatable workflows.

What we're looking for

  • Professional experience: 5+ years in blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, financial-crime or narcotics investigations, threat intelligence, or a comparable senior analytical role.

  • Blockchain tracing expertise: deep hands-on experience tracing funds across multiple blockchains and through laundering or obfuscation techniques such as mixers, chain-hopping, bridges, peel chains and layered cash-out behavior.

  • Investigative tradecraft: demonstrated ability to independently run complex investigations and synthesize findings into clear written intelligence products, including assessments, lead packages, fund-flow analysis and attribution reporting.

  • Strong communication: especially the ability to turn technically complex findings into understandable, actionable intelligence for government and private-sector audiences.

  • Judgment and execution: sound judgment and curiosity, and the ability to operate in a fast-moving environment where outputs must still stand up to scrutiny.

  • AI fluency: experience using AI tools and large language models to accelerate research and augment analytical workflows, with the ability to critically evaluate AI-generated outputs for accuracy and relevance.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in government, national security, law enforcement, or a mature private-sector investigations or threat intelligence program.

  • Familiarity with darknet markets, drug-trafficking networks, OTC and ATM laundering

  • Familiarity with OSINT and with combining blockchain activity with off-chain signals and adversary behavior.

  • Comfort with modern investigative tooling, including AI and structured data environments such as TRM, Maltego, Palantir or similar platforms.

About the Team

  • The team operates within TRM’s Blockchain Intelligence organization, alongside threat intelligence analysts, on-chain investigators, and law enforcement partners

  • Blockchain Intelligence Analysts are the operational core, converting on-chain tracing and off-chain intelligence into attribution and actionable leads on transnational criminal organizations

  • Distributed team with an async-first approach via Slack and Notion, plus structured syncs for alignment

  • High autonomy, high standards, low bureaucracy. You’ll work directly with analysts, engineers, and customers who depend on your output

 

Team Operating Rhythms

  • Weekly team syncs to align on priorities and review active casework

  • Regular async updates via Slack on active investigations, attribution work, and leads in flight

  • Primary time zone overlap: Working hours should overlap with both UK and US business hours

  • All output documented in Notion and TRM’s investigative tools

  • Surge availability expected when partners need a fast turnaround

 

Join Our Mission

We seek people whose work matters, who build with speed and rigor, and who take pride in protecting others through their craft. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, apply anyway.

 

Build to protect civilization. Let’s do it together.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

Senior Controls Engineer 

Parallel is seeking a Senior Controls Engineer with deep expertise in control systems development to join our engineering team. This role focuses on modeling, simulating, and designing the software that controls the electrical and mechanical systems on our rail vehicles, and on proving that software out in simulation before it reaches hardware.   • Develop and maintain plant models of vehicle dynamics, powertrain, and braking systems, and use them to analyze, simulate, and tune controllers in tools such as MATLAB/Simulink or Python

  • Build and own simulation infrastructure, including model-in-the-loop (MIL), hardware-out-of-the-loop (HOOTL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) environments, used to verify control software ahead of vehicle testing

  • Support system integration and vehicle testing, using simulation to reproduce and debug issues observed on hardware

  • In 30 days: You have defined requirements and an architecture for the platooning simulation suite. You have run the existing code and have developed a feature roadmap to achieve the analysis goals required for the project

You are running a test campaign using real Parallel vehicles to validate the outputs of the model and ground our software stack

  • State estimation (Kalman filtering, sensor fusion) and system identification from field data.
  • Robust control, or hybrid systems that combine continuous dynamics with discrete events like contact and impact.
  • NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Omniverse, or similar simulators such as Gazebo, MuJoCo, or Drake.

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.

We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.

About the Internship Program

Our internship programme gives early-career talent the opportunity to build practical skills, contribute to meaningful projects and learn alongside experienced colleagues in digital finance.

Typically lasting six months and based in our Brussels office (London possible), each internship includes hands-on experience, clear learning goals and dedicated guidance and regular feedback. We look for curiosity, relevant foundational skills, deep, active interest and passion for digital assets and the potential to grow exponentially with us - you don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Where performance, business needs and available opportunities align, an internship may lead to a permanent role, though this is not guaranteed.

We are looking for 3-4 high-caliber Quantitative Analyst Interns to sit within our Strategic Market Making (CeFi and DeFi), Credit and Corporate Development desks/teams (see other openings on our career page for details).

Application deadline: 30 November 2026
Start date: 1 March 2027


Selection process:

  • Interview with Talent Acquisition representative

  • Interview with Hiring Manager

  • Recruitment Challenge

 
 

The role

About Strategic Market Making Desk
Our Strategic Proprietary Market Making team researches and deploys systematic trading strategies across centralized digital asset venues. We study how order-book dynamics, fragmented liquidity, exchange design and participant behaviour shape pricing, execution and risk.

As a Quantitative Analyst Intern within the HFT track, you will work alongside quantitative researchers, traders and engineers to analyse market and trading data, test hypotheses through backtesting and simulation, and build tools that improve strategy performance and risk visibility. You will investigate how fair value, liquidity, latency, queue position, fees and adverse selection affect real-world execution across venues.

 

This is a technical and applied internship. We are looking for someone who combines strong quantitative reasoning and coding skills with a detailed understanding of electronic markets. You should be curious about how exchanges work beneath the interface and able to connect market microstructure to trading outcomes.



Key Responsibilities - Quantitative Analyst (HFT)

  • Analyse multi-venue top-of-book and depth data, trades, orders, fills and cancels to study liquidity, price discovery and execution quality.

  • Build and validate latency-aware, event-driven backtests with explicit assumptions around maker/taker execution, queue position, fill probability, fees and cancellations.

  • Measure spread capture, forward markouts, fees and adverse selection, and investigate how execution quality changes across venues, instruments and market regimes.

  • Build reusable Python tools and data pipelines using modern columnar analysis and SQL for strategy research, performance attribution and monitoring.

  • Study cross-venue price discovery, lead–lag relationships, fair-value construction and spot–perpetual basis while accounting for data staleness, instrument design and settlement-currency differences.

  • Support live strategies through PnL, inventory and exposure analysis, post-trade review and investigation of unexpected performance.

  • Evaluate liquidity-program economics by balancing execution quality, market share, fees and incentives, and work with traders and engineers to translate research into robust production improvements.

  • Present findings clearly, including assumptions, limitations, risks and recommended next steps.

Who You Are/Key Requirements - Quantitative Analyst (HFT)

  • Quantitative and coding foundations: You are pursuing or recently completed a degree in mathematics, computer science, engineering, physics, quantitative finance or a related field. You are proficient in Python for data analysis, ideally including Polars or similar columnar tools, and comfortable with SQL, Git and command-line workflows. Experience with ClickHouse or another analytical database is valuable.

  • Electronic market structure: You understand limit order books, order types, maker/taker mechanics, matching and priority rules, spreads, market depth and how trades move prices.

  • Execution awareness: You can reason about the order lifecycle from signal to acknowledgement and fill, including exchange APIs, latency, queue position, partial fills, cancellations, fees, slippage and adverse selection.

  • Digital asset markets: You understand key differences between spot and perpetual futures, including basis, funding, leverage, liquidation risk, settlement currencies and residual exposure.

  • Quantitative reasoning: You are comfortable with probability, statistics, time-series analysis and evaluating noisy results without overstating significance.

  • Hands-on curiosity: Ideally, you have built or analysed something yourself—such as an order-book study, trading bot, exchange connector, backtest, execution simulator or market-data pipeline.

  • Trading judgement: You naturally question whether an apparent edge survives latency, fees, market impact, changing liquidity and real execution constraints.

  • Ownership and communication: You can structure an ambiguous problem, test assumptions and communicate findings and limitations clearly in English.

 

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with exchange WebSocket/REST APIs and asynchronous market-data pipelines

  • Exposure to Rust or another systems programming language

  • Experience with tick/order-book data, event-driven simulation or execution modelling

  • A technical project demonstrating sustained interest in systematic trading or market microstructure

 

Our offer

  • A 6 month paid internship at world-renowned digital assets company with accommodation provided for entirety or part of it

  • The opportunity to learn about digital assets and blockchain from a 30,000 ft view of the entire ecosystem

  • Working from one of Brussels newest, nicest and most advanced office spaces

  • A global, collaborative and tech-driven environment.

  • Autonomy & Impact - our flat structure means you can contribute your ideas from day one and help shape the foundation that will power Keyrock’s future business.

  • Culture of Excellence - we value nimbleness, drive for success, owner mentality and collaboration.

  • Opportunity to leave your mark and start your career in one of the most reputable companies in the digital assets world

  • We are envisioning for the internship to be based pre-dominantly in Brussels. It is possible for a selected candidate to be based in London, UK, provided at least 1-2 months onboarding period would be spent in Brussels together with the rest of the interns cohort.

 

Our recruitment philosophy

We value self-awareness and powerful communication skills in our recruitment process. We seek fiercely passionate people who understand themselves and their career goals. We're after those with the right skills and a conscious choice to join our field. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who’s driven, collaborative, acts with ownership and delivers solid, scalable outcomes.

As an employer we are committed to building a positive and collaborative work environment. We welcome employees of all backgrounds, and hire, reward and promote entirely based on merit and performance.
